compatibility_adjustments.topic: torch wheel channel: official pin is torch==2.2.0+cu121, the project uses the repository CUDA 12.4 index
compatibility_adjustments.finding: The upstream requirements pin a CUDA 12.1 build (dgl 2.3.0+cu121 is the explicit marker). That build is not available from the repository's configured PyTorch index (https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124, envs/torch2/pyproject.toml:33-36) and the machine driver must be able to load the wheel. LatentFlow uses no CUDA-12.1-specific API: models/LatentFlow.py uses only nn.Conv1d, nn.GRUCell, nn.Linear, nn.LayerNorm, nn.Dropout, torch.topk/scatter/bmm/softmax/eye/masked_fill_ and Tensor.unfold, all of which are unchanged between torch 2.2 and 2.6; exp/exp.py:97-106 already falls back to torch.device('cpu') when torch.cuda.is_available() is false, and main.py:53-55 guards torch.cuda.set_device the same way.
compatibility_adjustments.resolution: torch is declared as ==2.6.0 and served from [tool.uv.sources] torch = { index = "pytorch-cu124" } / [[tool.uv.index]] name = "pytorch-cu124", url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124", explicit = true — i.e. the exact same wheel channel as the repository default environment envs/torch2/pyproject.toml:12-13,29-36. This keeps a single CUDA runtime in the workspace (no second ~2.5 GB cu121 runtime) and preserves CPU execution as documented.
compatibility_adjustments.impact: Numerical results may differ at the last-decimal level from a torch 2.2.0+cu121 run; no API, dtype or device semantic used by LatentFlow changed. Recorded instead of silently pinning a wheel that cannot be resolved here.

compatibility_adjustments.topic: official requirements.txt is a full workspace dump, not the method's dependency set
compatibility_adjustments.finding: The file pins 225 distributions covering the authors' whole benchmark workspace. Modules that no LatentFlow file imports: dgl==2.3.0+cu121 (:35), einops==0.8.0 (:38), torch-dct==0.1.6 (:199), torch-geometric==2.6.1 (:200), torchaudio==2.2.0 (:201), torchvision==0.17.0 (:204), triton==2.2.0 (:209), tensorflow==2.20.0, ray==2.46.0, wandb==0.23.1 (:219), clearml, dash==3.0.4 (:31), dash-bootstrap-components, sktime, tsfresh==0.21.1 (:211), tslearn==0.6.4 (:212), ema-pytorch, Cython==3.1.4 (:30), ujson, yarl, docker-pycreds, trimesh, etc. Grepping the full upstream tree for 'dgl', 'torch_geometric', 'einops', 'torch_dct', 'torchvision', 'tensorflow' and 'ray' returns only the requirements.txt lines themselves — no import anywhere in main.py, exp/, models/, layers/, data/ or utils/.
compatibility_adjustments.resolution: Only the distributions reachable from the LatentFlow import graph are declared: torch, numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, scipy, matplotlib, tqdm, vus, toml (+ easytsad). Everything else is omitted.
compatibility_adjustments.impact: Smaller, faster and far more reproducible lock (no tensorflow/ray/dgl/torch-geometric resolution, no Cython or dgl source builds). dgl in particular is unbuildable from PyPI for cu121 without the extra DGL wheel index, so including it would make `uv lock` fail for no functional gain.

compatibility_adjustments.finding: The official workspace pins NumPy 1.26.4, and the evaluation backend vus 0.0.6 (requirements.txt:218) predates NumPy 2. The LatentFlow code itself uses nothing NumPy-2-specific.
compatibility_adjustments.resolution: Declared as numpy>=1.26,<2 so the resolver cannot silently upgrade to NumPy 2.x, which would change the behaviour of the official evaluation stack.
compatibility_adjustments.impact: None on the method; keeps the official numerical behaviour.

compatibility_adjustments.finding: Exact pins (matplotlib==3.9.2, pandas==2.2.3, scikit-learn==1.5.1, scipy==1.13.1, tqdm==4.66.5) were captured from one machine and can conflict with EasyTSAD core's own ranges on 3.11.

compatibility_adjustments.impact: The lock, not the manifest, is the reproducibility record; resolved versions remain inside the official pins' minor series.

incompatibilities.detail: The official torch==2.2.0+cu121 / dgl==2.3.0+cu121 combination cannot be resolved from the configured CUDA 12.4 index, and dgl 2.3.0+cu121 additionally requires an external DGL wheel index. Neither package is imported by any LatentFlow module.
incompatibilities.mitigation: torch is taken from the repository's cu124 index at 2.6.0 (see compatibility_adjustments[0]); dgl, torch-geometric, torch-dct, torchvision, torchaudio and triton are omitted (compatibility_adjustments[1]). The documented CPU fallback in exp/exp.py:97-106 keeps the method runnable without a GPU.

incompatibilities.detail: The official evaluation metrics (Affiliation_F1 / VUS_ROC / VUS_PR) are computed with the external 'vus' package (upstream/README.md; upstream/utils/vus_evaluate.py:6-8). EasyTSAD/Evaluations ships its own VUS protocol (EasyTSAD/Evaluations/Protocols/VUS.py) but not the 'vus' distribution, so the method environment must install it explicitly.
incompatibilities.mitigation: vus==0.0.6 is a hard dependency of this project (pinned exactly as in upstream/requirements.txt:218); the controller's import check should confirm 'import vus.metrics' resolves inside environment/.venv.
